summary: You've got the drive and the brake pressed at the same time. You want to move, and something in you pulls back, so your energy comes out in fits, or grinds against a wall you can't quite name.
body: You've got the drive and the brake pressed at the same time. You want to move, and something in you pulls back, so your energy comes out in fits, or grinds against a wall you can't quite name. Action may come with hesitation here. Wanting something can bring up pressure, resistance, or the sense that desire has to justify itself first. You may push hard and burn out, or sit on the drive until it turns to frustration. The work is steady, deliberate effort, where the brake becomes control instead of a cage.
gift: At your best: disciplined, durable, able to finish what flashier people can't.
shadow: The trap: frustration, self-blocking, and anger that turns inward.
integration: Work with resistance instead of only fighting it. Pace, structure, and direct anger give your drive a path.
do: Channel the drive into one steady, long effort
Treat the brake as control, not a cage
dont: Let frustration calcify into giving up
